newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

YARD BLITZ WITH "ZERO TOLERANCE' Scotland Yard launches Operation Zero Tolerance today in the Kings Cross area. The US style police operation will involve 25 uniformed officers in a high visibility patrol. Previously considered 'low profile' offences such as begging, prostitution and drug dealing will be tackled in order to improve the quality of life for those who live, work and travel through the area.

An announcement is expected by the European Commission this week concerning the controversial link up between Lonrho and Anglo American. An full investigation is expected into allegations that Anglo American's purchase of a 26 percent stake in Lonrho would give the company's significant influence over the Lonrho's platinum mining operations.
CABBIES' SHARE FLOAT GETS THE GREEN LIGHT

Drivers of Computer Cab the radio black taxis network, have voted 344-220 in favour of a stock market flotation of the company. Floating on the Alternative Investment Market will raise about four million stg towards the cost of Mobistar satellite tracking system. Rebel drivers of the 2000 strong network have vowed to continue legal moves to halt the shares sale.

Today the credit card group Mastercard International unveiled plans for a $150 million (90 million stg) deal to purchase a 51 percent stake in Mondex International, the electronic smartcard developer.
Maurice Newman chairman of the Australian stock exchange has suggested that to solve some of its problems the London Stock Exchange undergo demutualisation.
